title: Chanticleer and Partlet: How Chanticleer and Partlet Went to Visit Mr Korbes
paragraphs: On another day Chanticleer and Partlet decided to go out for a ride together. Chanticleer built a handsome carriage with four red wheels and hitched six mice to it, and then he and Partlet climbed in and off they drove. Before long a cat met them and asked, “Where are you off to?” And Chanticleer answered,

“We’re on our way
A visit to pay
To Mr Korbes, the fox, today.”
Then the cat said, “Take me with you.” “Gladly,” said Chanticleer. “Climb up on the back, and make sure you don’t fall off.”

“Look after this fine coach of mine,
And keep my pretty red wheels clean!
Now, mice, get ready,
And, wheels, roll steady!
For we’re on our way a visit to pay
To Mr Korbes, the fox, today.”
Soon a millstone, an egg, a duck and a pin came along, and Chanticleer let them all climb into the carriage and ride with them.

When they got to Mr Korbes’s house, he was not at home. So the mice pulled the carriage into the coach-house, Chanticleer and Partlet flew up onto a beam, the cat settled down in the fireplace, the duck climbed into the washing tub, the pin stuck himself into the bed pillow, the millstone lay down across the top of the front door, and the egg rolled itself up in the towel.

When Mr Korbes came home, he went to the fireplace to build a fire, but the cat threw all the ashes in his eyes. He ran to the kitchen to wash, but there the duck splashed water all over his face. When he tried to dry himself, the egg broke to pieces in the towel, all over his face and eyes. Now he was very angry, and he went to bed without any supper. But when he laid his head on the pillow, the pin stabbed his cheek. At that he was absolutely furious, and he jumped up and would have run out of the house. But when he reached the door, the millstone fell on his head and killed him on the spot.
